turns.response_html:
Excessive licking of the teeth and face can indicate several things, including dental issues, nausea, allergies, anxiety, or a compulsive behavior.

You should take your Maltese puppy to the veterinarian to rule out a medical problem like dental pain or gastrointestinal upset. If medical issues are excluded, it may be due to stress, boredom, or attention-seeking behavior.

Would you like tips on how to manage possible anxiety or boredom in a puppy?

To reduce possible anxiety or boredom, focus on enrichment and redirection:

  • Increase Mental Stimulation: Use puzzle feeders, KONG toys stuffed with peanut butter or yogurt, or lick mats to make her work for food, which tires her out mentally.
  • Boost Exercise: Ensure she gets daily walks and playtime to burn off excess energy and stress.
  • Redirect Licking: When she starts licking, immediately give her an appropriate chew toy or a treat-filled toy to redirect the behavior.
  • Create a Safe Space: Give her a quiet, comfortable den (like a crate or cozy bed) where she can retreat when feeling stressed.

Remember to see your vet first to rule out any pain or medical issues, as a physical cause must be addressed.
